timeline.title: A Short History of New Year
items: In ancient Babylon, people welcomed the new year by promising the gods to pay debts and return what they borrowed.
The Julian calendar began the year on 1 January, named after Janus, the god who looks back and forward.
Robert Burns sent off the words of a song about old friends and days gone by. Now the world sings it at midnight.
A magazine first chose one person to sum up a whole year. The tradition still runs today.
today: Not in the history books yet. But for us, the year that mattered most.

letters.title: What the World Has Said About Time
items: We do not remember days, we remember moments.
The days are long, but the years are short.
Ring out the old, ring in the new, ring, happy bells, across the snow.
Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.
letters.hand: They all say it beautifully. We just say: what a year.

facts.title: The Science of a Year
items: In one year, the Earth carried you all about 940 million kilometres around the sun.
A heart beats roughly 35 million times a year. Plenty of those were for each other.
People are far more likely to laugh with others than alone. Laughter is made for sharing.
Busy years full of new experiences feel longer when we look back. So every adventure counts.
Smell is closely tied to memory. One scent can bring back a moment from years ago.
A year is about 365 and a quarter days long. That is why we get a leap year every four years.
facts.hand: Science can measure a year. It cannot measure how much happened in this one.

world.title: Why the World Was Better This Year
items: A kitchen that was never quiet.
More laughter than any year deserves.
Muddy boots by the door, and happy faces.

Stories that will be told for years.
And proof that the best things are done together.
world.close: {year} was better because of you, {who}. Here is to the next one.

note.title: What we believe a year is
paras: We make magazines for a living, and every December the year in review issues are the ones that make us smile most.
We believe a year is not only the big headlines. It is the ordinary Tuesdays, the burnt toast, the singing in the car, the hugs in the hallway. The little things that turn out to be the big ones.
{who}, someone wanted to keep this year safe. Not lost in a camera roll, but printed on pages you can pass around the table, laugh at and keep.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, it was a year full of love.
note.wish: Happy new year, {who}. May the next one be even better.
